prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identity of its active form, which made incretin-based treatment of diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: I keep a single-part B035 prize with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, so my preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1. The exchange confirmed that no one disputes merit or maturity: proglucagon processing, the insulinotropic truncated peptide, receptor biology in gut, pancreas and brain, and independent outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal disease form an unusually complete chain. Round 1 narrowed the open question to one seat and to framing, not to science. A prize for the physiology and the identity of the active form fits Physiology or Medicine, and it lets the therapy stand as the demonstration of the discovery rather than the object of the prize. The citation I propose names the hormone and its active form, so it describes what the three laureates actually established and does not claim credit for the drug-development step.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is still attribution, and I cannot remove it. Knudsen's design of long-acting analogues is decisive for the drugs patients receive, and a trio without her can read as a prize for the idea rather than the medicine. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) form is publicly contested, and Habener-type contributions sit outside the credited names, so any trio is open to challenge on fairness. I also concede the force of the chair's fourth question: under the three-person cap a second part is not possible without cutting a GLP-1 laureate, and I am not willing to cut Drucker or Holst, whom all six of us name. A one-part prize leaves B028, B014 and B047 for later years, and that cost is real even if it is acceptable.

responses.point: Marie keeps Knudsen in place of Mojsov, arguing that the prize should carry physiology through to long-acting analogues, and that three colleagues prefer Mojsov but the priority claim is contested.
responses.response: Her argument is the strongest one against my trio and it moved my thinking on the citation, though not on the names. I accept that Knudsen's work is the step that made a physiological hormone a drug. I still hold that the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine is best placed to credit the discovery of the hormone's active form and actions, and that the analogue step builds on it. Her contested-priority point is fair and I cannot settle it from the supplied files, so I rely only on what is in the round-1 record: Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active peptide is a credited contribution on the ballot, and the dispute concerns priority, not whether the work was done. If the committee decides the central achievement is the development of long-acting incretin therapy, her trio is the more coherent one, but I would then want the citation to say so, and the decision should be made on that stated principle and not drift toward it.

responses.point: Per, as chair, asks whether the third seat can be settled on verifiable evidence, whether one citation wording can be fair to both a Mojsov and a Knudsen trio, and whether a second part such as B047 is feasible. His round-1 ranking placed the unfolded protein response second.
responses.response: On verification, none of us can confirm the priority record from the supplied material, and I would not let an unverified claim in either direction decide the seat. That argues for a citation that states what is common ground, namely the physiology and the active form, and not one worded to pre-empt the dispute. On a combined wording, I do not think one sentence can be equally fair to both trios, because the choice of third name is the choice of what is honoured. On B047, I agree it is a clean and mature Mori and Walter pair, but with the three-person cap it can only enter by cutting Drucker, Holst or Mojsov, and I will not do that to a unanimous first choice. Its clinical consequence is also largely indirect, so I keep it as a later-year candidate and not as a second part now.

responses.point: Abdel names the same Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio, says he would build the prize around the discovery of the hormone and its active form rather than a single product, and sees B028 as a second-place alternative while noting that a second part is not possible without cutting GLP-1 credit.
responses.response: We agree on the trio and on the arithmetic of the cap. His point that the commercial character of the incretin success should not drive the choice is one I share, and it favours a physiology-led citation. I would add that a discovery-weighted prize is also the better defence against the charge that we are rewarding a pharmaceutical success story, since it credits the biology that any company or laboratory could then build on. On B028, I still place it as my first alternative because the two-person credit is compact and the clinical record is strong. I disclosed that RNA processing is my field, so I treat my enthusiasm for it with some caution and do not push it into the configuration.

responses.point: Thomas prefers a single-achievement prize built on the physiology, with Holst, Drucker and Mojsov, and lists B011 or B014 as candidates for a second part in a later round, noting upstream credit problems for both.
responses.response: I agree with the single-achievement preference, and with his reading of a discovery as a discernible change in a field. I share his concern about upstream credit for B011, where the cytogenetic and oncogene work sits outside the credited names, and for B014, where Eshhar's chimeric-receptor concept does. That is why I keep B014 only as an alternative and not as a second part, and why I rank B028 above B011 as a fallback: its credit is easier to state. A second part added this year would have to pay for itself in attribution clarity as well as merit, and none of the alternatives does so yet without cutting a GLP-1 laureate.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contested priority for the active GLP-1 peptide outweighs Knudsen's decisive development role. I cannot verify the priority record from the supplied files and my account rests on recollection of the literature.
Whether the committee, as a matter of principle, wants to honour discovery and physiology or also the drug-development step, which determines the third seat.
Whether the absence of Habener-type contributions from the credited names makes any B035 trio unfair enough to change the choice.
Whether B028 or B014 would be better placed than the current arithmetic allows if the committee decided to restructure B035 around two names, which I do not propose.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. My profile documents co-authorship with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén and research in single-cell RNA methods and RNA processing. None of the credited names on any shortlisted ballot is a documented collaborator. The overlap of my field with the antisense splicing candidate (B028), my first alternative, is a field overlap and not a personal tie, and I request no recusal.
